meaningMnemonic: This radical is the same as the kanji. It means below .

The kanji and the radical that look like this are exactly the same. They are both Asia . This can also mean sub- . As in subtropics, subspecies, subhuman… That kind of sub-! When it's not in a place name, 亜 will usually be using its sub- meaning. Hints 亜 is associated with Asia because of its あ reading, but sometimes you might see it used as ateji for other place names as well. And don't forget that sub- meaning!
readingMnemonic: What's the first sound in Asia ? It's A ( あ ). Nice and easy! Hints A is for Asia!

meaningMnemonic: The barracks radical and the barracks kanji are the same! Hints Know your radicals, yo!
readingMnemonic: Barracks are pretty big, so they weigh a ton ( とん ). And they probably take tons of materials to build. Hints Imagine trying to lift some barracks. They weigh a ton! How are you supposed to do this? Why would you even try to lift something that obviously weighs a couple tons?!

meaningMnemonic: You see a mountain in the shape of a turtle shell sticking out into the ocean. It's a cape ! No, not the kind you wear, the geographical kind. When you're on land, most capes look like turtle shell mountains sticking out into the sea. Do you know any capes like that near where you live? Hints Picture the turtle shell shaped cape. Feel the salty wind in your hair!
readingMnemonic: You decide to walk along this cape because it looks like the perfect place to get rid of your old me at sack ( みさき ). It's starting to smell, but the ocean breeze from the cape pulls the meat sack out of your hands and off into the sky (then probably into the sea too). Hints The next time you go to the cape, remember to bring your old, used meat sack. You can toss it right into the ocean and it won't bother you ever again! Just make sure no one sees you.

meaningMnemonic: You pour molten gold down three slide s while taking measurement s in order to make a cast of something. Whatever it is you're casting, it requires a lot of gold (three slides' worth!) and some very precise measurements. Hints Imagine yourself carefully pouring the gold down each of your three slides. Really be careful — the measurements need to be exact, or the cast won't come out right.
readingMnemonic: At last, you reveal what you've cast : a gold statue of Chew bacca ( ちゅう ). It's a life-size cast, which is why you needed so much gold and such exact measurements. Hints Picture your majestic Chewbacca cast. You place it outside your front door to guard the entrance to your house. Wraaaaaaarrrrrrr!

meaningMnemonic: You have to use your fingers to make an exit because you're so clumsy . You can't seem to get the door to open, your hands just slip around on the knob uselessly. Instead, you take your fingers and stick them into the door frame, pulling the whole thing off the hinges so you can leave. Hints Of course, you're too clumsy to do that right either, you accidentally threw the door backwards and hurt some people...
readingMnemonic: After you make your clumsy mistake you realize that these doors come in sets ( せつ ). And now you have to try to open another door. And another door. So many sets of doors! Hints Imagine trying to use your clumsy fingers all over the sets of doors. You keep falling over and hurting yourself. Why is it so hard to leave?!

meaningMnemonic: If you want to say how eternity sounds you have to compose a poem. Or an essay. Or a song. Recite those deep thoughts about eternity and impress everyone who hears it. Hints Try to compose a poem about eternity right now. Just jot it down somewhere.
readingMnemonic: You decide to compose a poem about an a corn ( えい ). The tiny acorn is the perfect vessel for you to say how eternity feels to you. Hints Let me recite the acorn poem to you now: Acorns start small Grow up big and tall Spread their baby acorns for all Live on for all eternity

meaningMnemonic: If a pilot manages to land under a canopy with a helicopter that's pierced with a sideways barb in the heart of winter you should congratulate them! People should always be congratulated for doing good things, and this is one of the best things you've ever heard of! Hints Can you imagine how difficult landing a helicopter is in just one of these horrible conditions? Congratulate them!
readingMnemonic: Congratulate the pilot with ca ke ( けい )! Hints Cake is always the appropriate celebratory food.

meaningMnemonic: You can only give a kiss of alcohol to dairy . If you add anymore than a kiss the dairy will curdle and you won't be able to drink it anymore. Bleh. Hints Imagine trying to give more than a kiss of alcohol to dairy and watch it bubble and curdle and get all gross and chunky.
readingMnemonic: Dairy isn't kept with other drinks, it needs to be placed on a rack ( らく ). I hope you've been using your dairy rack to store your dairy. If you haven't you should get one right away! Hints Look at all your dairy products: milk, yogurt, cheese, all of it sitting nicely on your dairy rack.

meaningMnemonic: If someone makes a bamboo horse , you know it's deliberate . You can't accidentally make an entire horse out of bamboo. Hints Someone sat down and deliberately planned the entire horse out, collected the materials, and made it by hand.
readingMnemonic: As you admire all the deliberate details in this bamboo horse, the ghost of Toku gawa ( とく ) Ieyasu appears before you! "I deliberately made this horse to show you how important being deliberate is. You should be absolutely certain and decisive about your decisions." Hints Tokugawa Ieyasu then poofs out of existence and so does the bamboo horse.

meaningMnemonic: Every leader will come to despise their followers. In the beginning everything is fine and dandy, but eventually the leader's followers will ask for more and more things, eventually ridiculous things, and the leader will really despise them for it. Hints Imagine yourself as a leader who's come to despise every single one of their followers. Look down at them in disgust as they ask you to grant them all a pony.
readingMnemonic: The more you despise them, the more boo ze ( ぶ ) you drink. This is not smart or healthy, but it's what this kind of hate does to people. Hints This is not a healthy way to handle things! If you despise someone you should talk to them, don't turn to booze. Don't be like every leader that's come before you.

meaningMnemonic: If there is dirt in a crab trap , it's a lot for the crabs to endure . Hints Imagine a little crab getting stuck in a crab trap with dirt and other crabs. Endure the horror as long as you can, little friend.
readingMnemonic: You decide to make the little crab that endure d being stuck in a dirty crab trap your pet, and put a colla r ( こら ) round its little neck. Hints Imagine yourself putting a collar around the crab's neck, then adding a leash and taking your crab for a walk around your neighborhood.

meaningMnemonic: A spirit wearing two mustache s must be evil . Everyone knows a mustache makes you evil, but two? And on a spirit? Yup, definitely evil. Hints Look at the evil spirit with two mustaches on its spirit face. Imagine its face in detail, especially those mustaches.
readingMnemonic: You're watching the evil mustache spirit when it starts to float toward your ca r ( か ). And it's... hey! It's trashing your car! You knew this guy was evil! Hints Imagine running around, flailing your arms, trying to get the spirit to stop ruining your car. But your hands go right through him and his two mustaches. You can't stop his evil doings.

meaningMnemonic: If you can stop a turkey by putting a spoon in its face you'll know it's a female turkey. A male turkey will peck the spoon out of your hand and run away. But a female turkey will wonder why you're putting a spoon there, stop, and look up at you wondering if you're okay. Hints Picture the female turkey stopping when it sees you holding out a spoon. Why are you doing that human? it thinks. Are you sick?
readingMnemonic: The female turkey then runs around making a mess ( めす ) of things trying to figure out what's wrong with you. She kicks around her hay, water bowl, and scratches at your pants, making more mess marks on them. But you don't move and she gets even more worried. Hints Imagine watching a female turkey make a mess of her own cage because she thinks you need help. How sweet.

meaningMnemonic: If you see someone eye ing your womb you're probably going to be weirded out by how friendly they're acting. You only let people who are really, really close to you look at your womb. So if this guy is acting that friendly he should have introduced himself first. Hints Imagine having someone you aren't friendly with trying to have a look at your womb. No thank you.
readingMnemonic: This friendly guy comes up to you and start to introduce himself, " ぼく -" but you stop him. He's been getting way too friendly with your womb and you don't want to hear who he is. He can ぼく at someone else, you're out. Hints Imagine only letting this guy start to introduce himself with ぼく before walking the heck outta there. Just because he was acting friendly doesn't mean he was actually your friend.

meaningMnemonic: If you stay up so long that you see the moon go down and the dawn come, people will say you have serious guts . It takes guts to stay up that late. More specifically, it takes a powerful gallbladder . Your gallbladder is sensitive to sleep changes, you know, so you risk a lot by staying up like that. Hints Imagine the guts you'd need to have to stay up so late that you see the moon and the sun switch places! And to risk gallbladder damage?! That takes guts!
readingMnemonic: You stayed awake outside for so long, just to prove you had guts and powerful gallbladder , that you also got a sweet tan ( たん ) out of it! Hints Imagine the deep tan you'd get after staying awake outside for such a long time. Tanning is also bad for your gallbladder! Man, you've really got guts to be getting tans like that.

meaningMnemonic: You try to use your fingers to cast doubt on people by using them to imitate each other. Right now you're using your fingers as finger puppets, imitating one of your friends to the others. Hints Picture your angry friend standing up next to your fingers, shouting, "I'm the real me! That's just an imitation!" The rest of your friends look nervously at each other. They doubt this person is real now.
readingMnemonic: Everyone thinks the friend you were trying to imitate is the imitation now and they have them in a gui llotine ( ぎ ). You even doubt if they're an imitation or if your fingers are the imitation. Hints Okay, so that's a lie, Your fingers are definitely imitating them, but you don't want to end up in the guillotine so you keep your mouth shut.

meaningMnemonic: What kind of tree is spicy ? A Japanese birch , or birch , obviously. There's nothing spicier than a Japanese birch! Hints Imagine licking the trunk of a Japanese birch tree and feeling the heat on your tongue.
readingMnemonic: You can only cut down a Japanese birch using a zoo saw ( あずさ ) because a regular saw can't handle how spicy these trees are. Hints Imagine using a zoo saw to cut down a Japanese birch tree. What's a zoo saw? It's a saw that's used in zoos, to build all the animal enclosures. And to cut down spicy trees.

meaningMnemonic: A tsunami hits a tree and your hat protects you from the water , but the hat itself is now covered in lacquer . You take it off and see that it's shiny and hard and protected. Hints Picture your hat and all of the other things the tsunami + tree water touched. It's all been hardened with a thick coating of the lacquer.
readingMnemonic: You decide to scoop up the rest of the lacquer water and use it on your furniture to protect it from your shih tzu ( しつ ). Now it can't bite or scratch or ruin any of your things anymore! Hints Watch as your shih tzu tries to bite your now lacquered chair. It gets its teeth around the leg, but it's hard as a rock. The shih tzu starts sneezing and spitting, letting go. Looks like it tastes bad too. Perfect!

meaningMnemonic: You see a gate with a tree growing through it and it reminds you that you need more leisure time. You walk up to the gate tree and curl up under its branches. No one will bother you because the tree is blocking the gate from being used. Hints Imagine spending your leisure time curled up under a tree that's growing through a gate. It's so cozy and secluded!
readingMnemonic: As you leisure ly nap, you hear a gruff voice, "Ah, you're done too, huh?" It's Genghis Khan ( かん )! He's spending his leisure time relaxing under this abandoned gate just like you. Hints But wait. Isn't Genghis Khan dead now? He winks at you, "Leisure time is for the dead." He smiles, and fades away, disappearing into the tree.

meaningMnemonic: You drop to the ground in a rice paddy , and then drop down in front of the cross you keep on you because you're trying to make yourself as lowly as you can in front of God. He said to lower yourself and this is the only way you can interpret that. Hints Imagine dropping down in a rice paddy, then again in front of your cross. Be as lowly as you can make yourself.
readingMnemonic: The only problem about being lowly is the he at ( ひ ). Everyone always told you that heat rises, but not here. The rice paddy is incredibly hot... unless oh no. Is that the heat of hell? Hints You tried to make yourself lowly in front of God but this heat is probably a sign that you didn't do it well enough.

meaningMnemonic: You meet a woman whose mouth is big and you instantly know this is the person you want to marry . Hints When you think about the person you want to marry, picture their mouth wide in a big, beautiful smile, a wide-open laugh. That's the lady for you, alright!
readingMnemonic: You marry this woman right away and you both go straight to an inn ( いん ) together! Hints When you get to the inn all you do is make her laugh and smile so you can bask in her bright, big, mouth smiles.

meaningMnemonic: If there are mountain s above and below you, that means you're on a mountain pass . Hints Imagine yourself walking along a mountain pass. Look up at the mountains above you, and down at the mountains below you.
readingMnemonic: It's only on this type of mountain pass that you'll be able to find the rare and adorable To kyo ge cko ( とうげ ). These tiny little critters can only be found on the ridges going above and below the mountains in Tokyo. There are like six mountains in Tokyo, so the next time you're scaling the ridges keep your eyes open for the Tokyo gecko! Hints Picture yourself hiking along a mountain pass in Tokyo and spotting a little Tokyo gecko run up and down on them. It's adorable and totally worth the climb.

meaningMnemonic: If you only let oneself (yourself) into your heart , you'll end up mourning all of the loves and friendships you could have had but didn't let in. Hints Picture yourself all alone. You never let anyone into your heart but yourself, and now you're mourning the life and friends you could have had.
readingMnemonic: While you're in mourning , you feel a sharp pain in your crying eyes. A key ( き ) comes sliding out with your tears. You look around wildly, but you're still alone. Is this... the key of mourning? Hints You try to push the key back into your body. Back into your eye, you even try to swallow it, but it comes back out. Finally you look down at your mourning heart and try the key there. It clicks. And opens.

meaningMnemonic: When under ground music makes it out into the light of the sun (the public), it finally becomes official . Music isn't really real unless people hear it outside of those secret underground concerts. Hints Think of all that music you listened to underground but not in the light of the sun. None of that was official music. None of it!
readingMnemonic: Once the music is official , you'll feel it in your sou l ( そう ). When you listen to it outside, under the bright sun, your soul gets to finally hear it too. Hints The official music penetrates into your soul, instead of just your ears, and it's affecting everyone else's souls too! Oh no... wait that's too many people. This was your song! No, it's too popular now, stop your souls from liking it! Ahhh!

meaningMnemonic: We want you to say things with your mouth right now because it's recital time! That poem you've been learning all week? Well it's time to recite it now, so hopefully you've learned it properly. Hints Open your mouth and start reciting now, it's recital time!
readingMnemonic: You've forgotten all the words to the poem you are meant to recite. To help with your recital , your guin ea ( ぎん ) pig hops onto your shoulder and whispers the words into your ear. Hints Picture your pet guinea pig hopping onto your shoulder, helping you and making sure the recital of your poem goes well.

meaningMnemonic: The stone that looks like a turkey boil ing underwater is just a reef . Hints It may seem like there are a bunch of turkeys under there, but it's just the shape the reef takes. Though I guess if you're looking from above the water it really does look like a bunch of turkeys freaking out.
readingMnemonic: The reef is the Shou gun's ( しょう ) favorite place to be nowadays. He sits next to the water, and stares down into it for hours. Hints You don't know if the Shougun likes the reef because he likes the beauty of the ocean, or if he's fantasizing about turkeys boiling. He's a... complex man.

meaningMnemonic: People think tsunami s are only made of water but they have a few pieces of sand in there too. There's actually more sand in the ocean than most people think. And tsunamis can't just have water and sharks in them. A few grains of sand will always slip in. Hints Imagine how those few grains of sand feel to get swept up into a tsunami. They didn't ask for this. They just wanted to stay at the bottom of the sea.
readingMnemonic: You already learnt the reading for 砂 , the other kanji for sand . It should be easy to remember this one too, since it's also さ ! Hints As long as you remember 砂 , you can remember さ .

meaningMnemonic: By putting flowers in a net , you manage to catch a canine ! But this just makes everyone scorn you. Hints Your scorn is well deserved — an upstanding member of society doesn't go around snatching up innocent flower-loving canines with a net. Go to the pet store and buy one like a normal person.
readingMnemonic: You notice everyone's scorn and respond by saying: "I bets ( べつ ) you I can catch me another one. I bets you I can." Hints Mistakenly assuming everyone is scorning you for not having caught enough canines, you go out to snatch up some more. Uh oh — I bets everyone is really gonna scorn you now!

meaningMnemonic: If the tsunami that's heading for your village is fat you should try to select a different one to hit instead. You don't want to select fat tsunamis because they do more damage. Hints Imagine being at the tsunami store and selecting the least fat one there.
readingMnemonic: If you're having trouble select ing which one is the least fat just check to see which tsunamis are eating ta cos ( た ). Only fat tsunamis will be eating them, so just look for one without a taco. Hints While you select the tsunami that's right for you. Keep an eye out for those fat taco-eating ones. And then stay away from them!

meaningMnemonic: Move thread in the right direction and you'll end up spinning it into yarn. Then you can spin that yarn into a sweater or a scarf with your favorite half tofu half fugu mascot on it! Hints Imagine spinning thread into whatever your imagination wants.
readingMnemonic: While you're spinning you realize that you've always wanted to make your own bow ling ( ぼう ) ball. And bowling ball cover. And bowling ball shoes. Hints Picture all of these thread-made bowling items. You're a really big bowling fan, huh?

meaningMnemonic: Going from a scooter to a helicopter that's big even for yourself ( oneself ), is a huge transition . Hints It's an upward transition, so that's nice, but it's still going to take you a long time to get used to using a big helicopter instead of a scooter.
readingMnemonic: You decide one transition isn't enough, so you transition to a cen taur ( せん ) too. Now you're a big half horse-half human creature and you'll fit in the big helicopter better. Hints A centaur is just a human halfway between transitioning into a horse, so it isn't even that hard to do!

meaningMnemonic: Making a mnemonic for a crab trap is VERY hard. So hard that I couldn't come up with one. But it's very possible that one of you will! Hints How hard is it to come up with a good mnemonic for a crab trap? Very hard!
readingMnemonic: You know what else is very something? Jean s ( じん ). Jeans are very expensive. Jeans are very tight. Jeans are very popular. Jeans are very a lot of things. Hints How many sentences can you make with very and jeans? More than me I hope.

meaningMnemonic: The tsunami that is good . This fabled creature has never been seen, but you wander the lands in search of it. Hints You wander everywhere, with no particular direction in mind.
readingMnemonic: As you wander , you come across a clue. It is fish roe ( ろう ). Hints Wherever the good tsunami goes, it leaves delicious fish roe behind. That's what makes it a good tsunami.

meaningMnemonic: In the side of a mountain , you carve out a roof with your jackhammer so you can worship the gods. Basically, you've created a little alcove where you can set up an altar and worship like some kind of mountain ascetic. Hints Worshippers of ages past had to spend years chipping away at the mountainside with pickaxes and shovels to build roofed spaces like this. Your jackhammer allowed you to save precious time and get right to worshipping.
readingMnemonic: What's the object of your worship ? Sou p ( すう )! There's a whole pantheon of soup gods, and you've come to the mountains to spend your days worshipping each and every one of them. Hints The Gazpacho Goddess, the Borscht Bodhisattva, the Minestrone Messiah… Each major soup variety has its own deity, so your worship schedule is pretty tight.

meaningMnemonic: A reef in the shape of a loop is an atoll . If you don't know what that is, it's a circular coral reef .
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: その時、日本のマグロ漁船「第五福竜丸」がたまたまビキニ環礁を航行しており、乗組員が被ばくしてしまった。
sentences.english: The Japanese tuna boat "S.S. Lucky Dragon 5" accidentally sailed around Bikini Atoll and the crew was exposed to radiation.

meaningMnemonic: Remember how you learned that 一遍 means "once?" Well if you add に and make it an adverb, it becomes at once .
readingMnemonic: This has the same reading you learned with 一遍 so you should be able to remember this too!

sentences.japanese: 一遍にいろんなことを言われても、分からないわ。
sentences.english: If you say a bunch of things at once I won’t understand.

meaningMnemonic: If you can congratulate someone for an occurrence in their life, it must be an auspicious event . You'll remember this happy event for a long, long time. 慶事 is a very formal word used to refer to an auspicious event, such as a wedding, the birth of a child, or other significant celebrations. You might encounter 慶事 in official announcements or formal congratulatory messages.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 親しい友人の慶事は自分のことの様にうれしい。
sentences.english: The happy events my close friends have make me as happy as if they were my own.

meaningMnemonic: Japanese birch river is Azusa River or simply Azusagawa . Azusagawa is both the Japanese name for the Azusa River, and a Japanese family name.
readingMnemonic: You learned both of these readings with the kanji. You just need to remember that rendaku turns かわ into がわ .

sentences.japanese: 普段の梓川はとても穏やかです。
sentences.english: The Azusa River is usually very calm.

sentences.japanese: 週末は梓川の水の透明感に癒やされてきました。
sentences.english: At the weekend, I was soothed by the clarity of the water in Azusa River.

sentences.japanese: 梓川さんの歌唱力が高いのは勿論だけど、曲の歌詞もすごくいいんだよね。
sentences.english: Of course, Azusagawa-san is a talented singer, but the lyrics of her songs are also really good.

meaningMnemonic: You should congratulate a person who speaks lots of dialect s because they have to be a really strong person , just like Mr. Benkei was. You think learning Japanese is hard now, just wait till you hear Osaka-ben and Hokkaido-ben. It takes a really strong person — a Benkei — to learn all those dialects, so congratulate them and tell them how strong they are! 弁慶 is the name of a Japanese historical figure who was really strong, so Benkei is the Japanese equivalent of Hercules or Achilles in Western languages.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: 弁慶と牛若丸は清水寺で戦いました。
sentences.english: Benkei and Ushiwakamaru fought at Kiyomizu Temple.

sentences.japanese: 家では威張っているが、外では従順になる人のことを「内弁慶」と言う。
sentences.english: A person who is arrogant at home but submissive outside the home is called an "uchi-benkei".

sentences.japanese: むこうずねは、ぶつけると弁慶ほど強い人でも涙を流すほど痛いことから、「弁慶の泣き所」といわれています。
sentences.english: The shin is known as "Benkei's weeping spot" because, if you hit it, it hurts so much that even someone as strong as Benkei would shed tears.

meaningMnemonic: If you have grief in your eye s, it means you've gone through a lot of bitterness and misery . You can always see in someone's eyes if they've experienced it too. You'll see this word most often in 憂き目を見る and 憂き目に合う , which both mean "to experience hardship ."
readingMnemonic: This word uses one of the kun'yomi readings for the kanji. You haven't learned this kun'yomi reading for 憂 , so here's a mnemonic to help you remember it: Why the bitterness in your eyes? You visited a famed u ni ( う ) restaurant, only to find it closed and locked. And as a lover of uni, you know no greater misery than to miss out on some uni.

sentences.japanese: 失恋の憂き目に遭いました。
sentences.english: I met with the misery of a broken heart.

meaningMnemonic: If you have really big guts you're a super bold and daring person. In fact, you might even be superman. That's how big your guts are. Don't worry, I don't tell anyone I know who you are. It'll be our little secret.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You should be able to read this on your own.

sentences.japanese: グループは、大胆にも真っ昼間から犯行に及んだのです。
sentences.english: The group is bold to commit crimes in broad daylight.

meaningMnemonic: What is a bud doing? It's budding ! Literally, what else can a bud be doing except budding? Moe is also a slang term for feelings of infatuation or affection that "bud" up in you, usually toward cute fictional characters. It can be an adjective to describe said cutesy characters too, especially ones you see in anime, manga, and video games. The term's a bit dated now, but 萌え is an important concept in otaku subcultures.
readingMnemonic: This word uses a kun'yomi reading you didn't learn with the kanji, so here's a mnemonic: You feel a budding of affection for the character Moe ( も ). Yes, the old bartender character from The Simpsons. He's so cute and moe with that apron and curly hair of his, you feel a deep, protective love toward him.

sentences.japanese: 萌え系
sentences.english: moe style

sentences.japanese: 萌えアニメ
sentences.english: moe anime

sentences.japanese: 萌えキャラ
sentences.english: moe character

sentences.japanese: 萌えポイント
sentences.english: moe score, moe points

sentences.japanese: 萌え要素
sentences.english: moe elements

sentences.japanese: このアカウントでは、萌え系を中心に、僕の好きなアニメや漫画を紹介していきます。
sentences.english: This account introduces some of my favorite anime and manga characters, especially the moe kind.

sentences.japanese: この仕草は、萌えポイントが高い。
sentences.english: This behavior scores really high on the moe cuteness scale.

sentences.japanese: このアニメは萌え要素が多いんだよね。
sentences.english: This anime has a lot of moe elements.

sentences.japanese: この作品はストーリーもいいけど、何より萌えキャラが魅力的だ。
sentences.english: The story of this work is great, but what really stands out are the adorable characters.

meaningMnemonic: The kanji and the word are exactly the same. That means they share meanings as well. 岬 means cape , which is a piece of land jutting out into the sea. While 崎 is mostly used in place names and compound words, 岬 can be used as a standalone noun, although you also see it in place names such as 宗谷岬 (Cape Sōya).
readingMnemonic: This has the same reading as the kanji you learned, meaning you know the reading!

sentences.japanese: 岬の突端にカフェがあるんです。
sentences.english: There's a cafe on the tip of the cape.

meaningMnemonic: If you want to create a cast you need to learn casting first. Then you can make lots of neat art, crafts, and counterfeit money. Wait, no, don't do that last one.
readingMnemonic: This is a jukugo word that uses the on'yomi readings of the kanji. You've learned both of them, so you should already know this word!

sentences.japanese: ここで、プラチナ・コインの鋳造をします。
sentences.english: Platinum coins are cast here.

Or, more figuratively, to feel down . 凹む is used in a physical sense when the surface of something is dented, collapsed inward, or features some kind of hollow depression. That can be anything from a dented car to even a fit, slimmed-down belly (sort of like the flab is "dented" in). In a figurative sense, 凹む is used when you're feeling down.
